questions.question: Who is the cabinet minister of the Union Ministry of Steel as of September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**HD Kumaraswamy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **HD Kumaraswamy** is a senior Indian politician and a former Chief Minister of Karnataka. He is a prominent leader of the **Janata Dal (Secular)** (JD(S)) political party.
 
• As of **September 2024**, he holds the position of the **Union Cabinet Minister of Steel**. His appointment reflects the government’s focus on enhancing the steel industry in India.
 
• The Ministry of Steel is responsible for formulating policies related to the growth, development, and regulation of the **steel industry** in India. It ensures the availability of steel for various sectors, including construction, infrastructure, and manufacturing.
 
• **HD Kumaraswamy** has been actively working to promote the domestic steel industry, ensuring the production of high-quality steel and encouraging investments from private and public sectors. *Hence, this makes him the correct option for the question.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union Ministry of Steel:**

 
 
• The **Ministry of Steel** was established to oversee the development and regulation of the steel industry in India. It formulates policies to ensure the growth of the sector.
 
• India is the **second-largest producer of steel** globally, making the role of the Ministry crucial in maintaining this position and ensuring sustainability in production and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Ministry of Steel:**
 
 
• The Ministry ensures adequate production and distribution of steel to meet the demands of various sectors like **infrastructure, defense, and manufacturing.**
 
• It supports **research and development (R&D)** to encourage innovative technologies that enhance production efficiency and reduce environmental impact.
 
• It regulates and coordinates efforts to maintain the international competitiveness of India’s steel industry.
 
 
 
• **About HD Kumaraswamy:**
 
 
• **HD Kumaraswamy** was born on **16 December 1959** in Karnataka. He is the son of former Prime Minister **H.D. Deve Gowda**.
 
• He served as the **Chief Minister of Karnataka** on two occasions, displaying strong administrative skills and a focus on rural development.
 
• As a politician, he has been known for his focus on promoting industries, infrastructure development, and enhancing the welfare of farmers and the rural population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India’s Steel Industry:**

 
 
• India’s steel industry plays a pivotal role in the country’s **economic growth**, contributing significantly to GDP and employment generation.
 
• India has a production capacity of around **154 million tonnes** of steel as of **2023**. The government is actively working on initiatives to achieve **300 million tonnes** of steel production capacity by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• India is a major player in the global steel market, competing with nations like **China, Japan, and the United States** in terms of production and exports.
 
• The **National Steel Policy** of **2017** aims to make India self-reliant in steel production while maintaining sustainability and environmental efficiency.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an aim of the Microfinance institutions in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decreasing the household income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Microfinance institutions (MFIs)** play a crucial role in providing financial services to underserved populations, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas of **India**.
 
• The primary objectives of MFIs include **promoting socio-economic development, empowering women, and achieving financial inclusion**. These aims are achieved by enabling access to small loans, savings, insurance, and other financial products. *Hence, statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct.*
 
• MFIs often focus on **promoting women empowerment**, as women are considered crucial drivers of socio-economic progress. Loans provided to women help improve household income, education, and healthcare access. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• One of the critical goals of MFIs is to **achieve financial self-sufficiency**. This ensures that the institution can sustain itself while offering affordable financial services to the needy. &

questions.question: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2024 is intended to add which of the following scheduled tribes to the list of Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khond Porja**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Amendment) Bill, **2024** seeks to amend the list of Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh. One of the notable additions is the inclusion of the **Khond Porja** tribe.
 
• The **Khond Porja** is an indigenous tribal community living predominantly in Andhra Pradesh. They are known for their unique traditions, culture, and social practices.
 
• The recognition of Khond Porja as a Scheduled Tribe provides them access to specific constitutional safeguards, reservations, and welfare schemes aimed at improving the socio-economic conditions of tribal communities. *Hence, the correct option is Khond Porja.*
 
• The addition of Khond Porja to the Scheduled Tribes list will ensure improved representation in government jobs, educational institutions, and legislative bodies, as per the provisions under **Article 342** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The list of Scheduled Tribes in each state is periodically revised to include or exclude communities based on their socio-economic status and cultural practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scheduled Tribes and Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes** are recognized under **Article 342** of the Constitution of India. It defines Scheduled Tribes as specific communities that are deemed to require special attention and support from the government.
 
• The President of India specifies the Scheduled Tribes list for each state and union territory through public notification. Parliament may later amend this list.
 
 
 
• **Khond Porja Tribe:**
 
 
• The **Khond Porja** tribe is one of the many indigenous communities residing in Andhra Pradesh. They are primarily engaged in agricultural activities and exhibit distinct cultural practices.
 
• The inclusion of the Khond Porja tribe under Scheduled Tribes status will facilitate access to welfare schemes such as scholarships, healthcare, housing, and job reservations.
 
• **Example:** Welfare schemes like the **Post-Matric Scholarship** for Scheduled Tribe students aim to promote higher education among tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Scheduled Tribes List:**
 
 
• The Scheduled Tribes list ensures the protection and preservation of tribal culture, languages, and rights while addressing socio-economic disparities.
 
• Being included in the Scheduled Tribes list enables communities like Khond Porja to demand representation in policy-making and governance structures.
 
• The government’s focus on tribal welfare is strengthened through measures like the **Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana** and other development programs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Article 342:**

 
 
• **Article 342** empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Tribes in various states and union territories after consulting with the respective state governments.
 
• Parliament holds the authority to amend the Scheduled Tribes list as required to address changing socio-economic dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes Welfare in India:**
 
 
• Various constitutional safeguards and programs like **Article 15(4)** and **Article 46** ensure the promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Tribes.
 
• The formation of tribal-dedicated ministries like the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** has strengthened tribal welfare efforts in India.
 
• Legislative measures such as the **Forest Rights Act (2006)** aim to protect the rights of Scheduled Tribes over forest land and resources.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution permits the State to make special provisions for women and children?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 15(3)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 15(3)** of the **Indian Constitution** permits the State to make special provisions for **women and children**.
 
• This article is part of **Article 15**, which generally prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. However, Clause (3) provides an exception by allowing the State to create provisions for their welfare.
 
• The goal of **Article 15(3)** is to ensure the upliftment of **women and children**, who are often vulnerable and marginalized in society. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The provision aligns with the broader principles of **social justice and equality**, ensuring that the state can take affirmative measures to protect the rights and welfare of women and children.
 
• Examples of such provisions include **reservation of seats in educational institutions** for women, special schemes for child welfare, and protection laws for women like the **Maternity Benefits Act**. *Hence, the correct statement is Article 15(3).*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 15 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 15** is a fundamental right that prohibits discrimination on the grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.**
 
• It includes specific clauses, such as **Article 15(3),** which allows the State to make special provisions for women and children, and **Article 15(4)**, which focuses on the advancement of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and socially and educationally backward classes.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Article 15(3):**
 
 
• It plays a crucial role in promoting **gender equality** and protecting the rights of women and children.
 
• The provision enables the State to implement laws such as the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act**, **Protection of Children from Sexual Offenses Act (POCSO)**, and special employment or educational schemes for women.
 
• **Example:** The **reservation for women** in Panchayati Raj institutions or the **National Nutrition Mission** focusing on child and maternal health.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other Articles:**
 
 
• **Article 14:** Provides for equality before the law and equal protection of laws.
 
• **Article 19:** Focuses on the right to freedom of speech and expression, but does not specifically mention provisions for women and children.
 
• **Article 21:** Guarantees the right to life and personal liberty, but **Article 15(3)** is more specific regarding affirmative actions for women and children.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Framework Supporting Article 15(3):**

 
 
• Several laws and schemes like the **Maternity Benefits Act**, **Equal Remuneration Act**, and **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)** are derived from the provisions of Article 15(3).
 
• **Reservation for women:** Many educational institutions and government jobs reserve seats for women to ensure their inclusion and empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Similar provisions for women and children exist in international frameworks like the **Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW)** and **United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC).**

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for the original Jurisdiction of the supreme court over Centre-State and Inter-State disputes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 131**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 131** of the **Indian Constitution** provides the **Supreme Court with original jurisdiction** in cases of disputes between the **Centre and State(s)**, or between two or more states.
 
• This jurisdiction is exclusive and allows the Supreme Court to directly entertain such cases without requiring them to be initiated at lower courts.
 
• Disputes under **Article 131** typically involve issues of **constitutional interpretation**, such as conflicts over legislative powers, financial matters, or administrative authority. *Hence, the correct option is Article 131.*
 
• **Article 130** refers to the **seat of the Supreme Court** and its ability to function anywhere in India as decided by the Chief Justice of India with the President’s approval. *This is not related to original jurisdiction. Hence, it is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 135** deals with the power of the Supreme Court to entertain cases under pre-Constitution laws unless Parliament provides otherwise. *This does not pertain to original jurisdiction over Centre-State or inter-State disputes. Hence, it is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 134** relates to appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in criminal cases, not original jurisdiction. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 131 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 131 **empowers the Supreme Court to adjudicate disputes between the **Government of India and one or more states**, or between states.
 
• The disputes must involve **legal rights and obligations**, not political disagreements or policy matters.
 
• For example, the Supreme Court has exercised its jurisdiction under this Article in cases involving **water-sharing disputes** between states like Punjab and Haryana.
 
 
 
• **Other Articles Related to Supreme Court Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• **Article 130:** Determines the seat of the Supreme Court.
 
• **Article 134:** Deals with appellate jurisdiction in criminal cases.
 
• **Article 135:** Grants the Supreme Court jurisdiction over pre-Constitution laws.
 
 
 
• **Important Examples of Disputes:**
 
 
• **State of Karnataka vs State of Andhra Pradesh:** A dispute regarding water-sharing of the Krishna River.
 
• Disputes regarding taxation powers between the Centre and States have also been resolved under Article 131.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conditions for invoking Article 131:**

 
 
• The dispute must involve **legal rights**, not political or administrative issues.
 
• The **Supreme Court** cannot entertain cases under Article 131 unless the matter directly relates to a constitutional provision.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Article 131:**
 
 
• Ensures the **federal balance** by resolving disputes between the Centre and States.
 
• Helps in maintaining the **constitutional framework** and interpreting laws effectively.
 
• Strengthens the role of the **Supreme Court** as the guardian of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which group 17 element gets its name for being a yellow-green dense gas with a choking smell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorine** is a chemical element represented by the symbol **Cl** and has an atomic number of **17**. It belongs to the group 17 elements, also known as the **halogens**.
 
• Chlorine is characterized as a **yellow-green dense gas**, which is highly reactive and has a distinctive **choking smell**. This smell is a result of its high reactivity and toxicity.
 
• It is widely used as a disinfectant in water treatment due to its ability to kill bacteria and other pathogens. *Hence, the statement correctly identifies chlorine as the element.*
 
• **Chlorine** was discovered in **1774** by Swedish chemist **Carl Wilhelm Scheele**. He obtained it by reacting hydrochloric acid with manganese dioxide.
 
• Chlorine is a crucial element used in various industries, including the production of **PVC (polyvinyl chloride)**, solvents, and other chemicals. *Hence, chlorine is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Halogens (Group 17 Elements):**

 
 
• Group 17 elements are known as **halogens**, which include **fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, and astatine**.
 
• Halogens are highly reactive non-metals and are often found in compounds rather than in their elemental forms due to their high reactivity.
 
• They form salts when they react with metals, which is why their name "halogen" means "salt-former" in Greek.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Chlorine:**
 
 
• Chlorine is extensively used in **water purification** to make drinking water safe by killing harmful microorganisms.
 
• It is a key component in the production of **PVC**, which is used in pipes, cables, and construction materials.
 
• Chlorine compounds are used in the manufacturing of pesticides, solvents, and medicines.
 
 
 
• **Physical and Chemical Properties of Chlorine:**
 
 
• Chlorine is a **diatomic molecule** (Cl₂) in its elemental form. It has a pungent smell and yellow-green color.
 
• It is highly reactive and combines with many elements and compounds. It is also a strong oxidizing agent.
 
• Chlorine is produced industrially via the **chlor-alkali process**, where sodium chloride solution is electrolyzed to produce chlorine gas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Options:**

 
 
• **Krypton:** Krypton is an inert gas and does not have a yellow-green color or a choking smell. It is used in lighting and photography.
 
• **Argon:** Argon is another inert gas and is used primarily in welding and lighting. It lacks the yellow-green color and choking smell characteristic of chlorine.
 
• **Helium:** Helium is a colorless, odorless gas, used in balloons and as a coolant. It does not match the description provided in the question.
 
 
 
• **Historical Usage:**
 
 
• Chlorine gas was used in **World War I** as a chemical weapon due to its toxic properties.
 
• Today, its controlled usage in water purification and industrial processes makes it invaluable.

questions.question: Which of the following sites is linked to the Indus Valley Civilisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohenjo-Daro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro** is one of the major urban centers of the **Indus Valley Civilisation**, which is considered one of the world’s earliest urban civilizations.
 
• It is located in present-day **Sindh province of Pakistan** and was rediscovered in **1922** by archaeologist **R.D. Banerji**.
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro** is known for its advanced urban planning, including a **grid system layout**, sophisticated **drainage system**, and well-constructed residential and public buildings. *Hence, it is directly linked to the Indus Valley Civilisation.*
 
• Other sites like **Ajanta, Sanchi, and Bhimbetka** are significant for Indian history but belong to different historical periods and are not associated with the Indus Valley Civilisation.
 
• **Ajanta:** Known for its Buddhist cave paintings and sculptures, dating back to **2nd century BCE to 6th century CE**.
 
• **Sanchi:** Famous for its **Buddhist stupas**, especially the Great Stupa, constructed during Emperor **Ashoka’s reign** (3rd century BCE).
 
• **Bhimbetka:** Known for its rock shelters and cave paintings, which date back to the **Paleolithic and Mesolithic ages**.
 
• These sites are historically significant but are not connected to the Indus Valley Civilisation. *Hence, the correct answer is Mohenjo-Daro.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indus Valley Civilisation:**

 
 
• The **Indus Valley Civilisation** (also known as Harappan Civilisation) existed from approximately **3300 BCE to 1300 BCE**. It was primarily located in the northwestern regions of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The civilization is notable for its **urban planning, advanced drainage systems, standardized weights and measures, and trade networks.**
 
• Major sites include **Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan, and Rakhigarhi**.
 
 
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro:**
 
 
• The name **Mohenjo-Daro** translates to "**Mound of the Dead**" in Sindhi.
 
• Key features include the **Great Bath**, which is believed to have been used for ritualistic purposes, and the **Granary**, which indicates organized storage and trade.
 
• Artifacts like seals, beads, tools, and pottery found here provide insights into the life and culture of the Harappan people.
 
 
 
• **Other Sites:**
 
 
• **Ajanta:** Located in Maharashtra, it is renowned for its **Buddhist art** and cave architecture.
 
• **Sanchi:** Situated in Madhya Pradesh, it is a key site for Buddhist architectural heritage, particularly from the Mauryan Empire.
 
• **Bhimbetka:** Found in Madhya Pradesh, it houses prehistoric cave paintings and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **Rediscovery of Mohenjo-Daro:**

 
 
• Discovered in **1922** by **R.D. Banerji** during excavations led by the Archaeological Survey of India.
 
• It is one of the best-preserved urban sites of the **Indus Valley Civilisation**.
 
 
 
• **Decline of Indus Valley Civilisation:**
 
 
• Factors like **climate change, shifts in river courses, and possibly invasions** contributed to its decline around **1300 BCE**.
 
• However, the exact reasons for its decline remain a subject of ongoing research.

questions.question: Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan was launched by whom in 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prime Minister of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan** was launched on **June 20, 2020**, by the **Prime Minister of India**, **Narendra Modi**. This initiative was aimed at providing immediate employment opportunities to migrant workers who had returned to their home states due to the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
• The program was implemented in **116 districts** across six states: **Bihar**, **Uttar Pradesh**, **Madhya Pradesh**, **Rajasthan**, **Odisha**, and **Jharkhand**. These districts were selected based on the concentration of migrant workers.
 
• The initiative aimed to ensure the **economic empowerment** of migrant workers by providing them with **local employment opportunities** through various government schemes. *Hence, the correct answer is Prime Minister of India.*
 
• Under this program, **25 types of infrastructure projects** were undertaken, including **construction of roads**, **housing**, **plantation**, **water conservation**, and **community development**, among others. These projects were carried out under different **central and state government schemes**.
 
• An estimated **Rs. 50,000 crores** was allocated for the implementation of the scheme, ensuring both **employment generation** and the creation of durable infrastructure.
 
• The program also provided a platform for **skilled, semi-skilled, and unskilled workers** to find employment opportunities in their home states, thereby reducing their dependency on jobs in urban centers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan:**

 
 
• The primary objective of the program was to provide **immediate employment** to returning migrant workers affected by the **COVID-19 lockdown**.
 
• It aimed to create **durable assets** in rural areas, which would contribute to the long-term development and infrastructure improvement in these regions.
 
 
 
• **Implementation and Monitoring:**
 
 
• The initiative was coordinated by **12 ministries** of the central government, ensuring the convergence of various schemes.
 
• The program was monitored using **geo-tagging** and **mobile applications** to track the progress of projects and ensure accountability.
 
 
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• The initiative focused on promoting **self-reliance** by providing **skill development** opportunities to migrant workers.
 
• It also emphasized the importance of **local employment generation**, which reduced the need for migration to urban areas for work.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Abhiyan:**

 
 
• The scheme played a vital role in addressing the challenges posed by the **reverse migration** of workers during the pandemic.
 
• It contributed to improving **livelihood opportunities** in rural areas, thereby reducing economic distress among migrant workers.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• The program created **employment opportunities** for millions of workers and helped in the development of infrastructure in rural districts.
 
• It highlighted the importance of **converging government schemes** to achieve comprehensive development goals.

questions.question: Name the singer who rose to prominence after recording the song 'Ishq wala love', which was released in the year 2012.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neeti Mohan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neeti Mohan** is a renowned Indian playback singer who gained significant recognition for her song **'Ishq Wala Love'**, which was released in the movie **Student of the Year** in **2012**.
 
• She is known for her melodious voice and versatility in singing across different genres like Bollywood, classical, and pop.
 
• **'Ishq Wala Love'** became immensely popular among audiences, contributing to Neeti Mohan's rise to fame. *Hence, option 2 is correct.*
 
• Neeti Mohan has received critical acclaim for her singing and has won multiple awards for her contribution to Indian music, including the **Filmfare RD Burman Award for New Music Talent** in **2013**.
 
• She is also a trained classical singer and has performed in numerous concerts across the globe, showcasing her talent and versatility.
 
• The song **'Ishq Wala Love'** was composed by **Vishal-Shekhar** and became one of the highlights of the movie **Student of the Year**, directed by **Karan Johar**.
 
• The movie was a commercial success, and the song played a significant role in establishing Neeti Mohan as a notable playback singer in Bollywood. *Hence, the correct answer is Neeti Mohan.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Neeti Mohan's Career:**

 
 
• Neeti Mohan started her career after winning the reality show **Popstars**. She became part of the band **Aasma**, which gained popularity in the early 2000s.
 
• She transitioned into playback singing and became a household name with hit songs like **'Jiya Re'** from **Jab Tak Hai Jaan** and **'Saadi Galli Aaja'** from **Nautanki Saala**.
 
• Neeti has collaborated with various renowned music directors like **A.R. Rahman**, **Vishal-Shekhar**, and **Pritam**, showcasing her ability to adapt to different musical styles.
 
 
 
• **About the Song 'Ishq Wala Love':**
 
 
• The song is a romantic number from the movie **Student of the Year**, which starred **Alia Bhatt, Varun Dhawan, and Sidharth Malhotra**.
 
• It was composed by **Vishal-Shekhar** and beautifully sung by **Neeti Mohan, Shekhar Ravjiani, and Salim Merchant**.
 
• The lyrics were penned by **Anvita Dutt**, and the song's relatable theme resonated with young audiences, making it a chartbuster.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Alka Yagnik:** A legendary playback singer known for her melodious voice and iconic songs like **'Taal Se Taal Mila'** and **'Agar Tum Saath Ho'**. However, she did not sing **'Ishq Wala Love'**.
 
• **Sunidhi Chauhan:** Another celebrated singer known for her energetic and versatile singing style. She has sung songs like **'Sheila Ki Jawani'** and **'Dhoom Machale'**, but she is not associated with **'Ishq Wala Love'**.
 
• **Jasleen Royal:** A contemporary singer and songwriter known for songs like **'Din Shagna Da'** and **'Nachde Ne Saare'**. She did not sing **'Ishq Wala Love'** either.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Recognition for 'Ishq Wala Love':**

 
 
• The song **'Ishq Wala Love'** became a defining moment for Neeti Mohan's career, earning her widespread recognition and appreciation.
 
• It showcased her ability to deliver a soft and melodious romantic track, contrasting her previous energetic numbers.
 
 
 
• **Neeti Mohan's Achievements:**
 
 
• She has won several accolades, including the **Filmfare RD Burman Award**, and has been nominated for multiple awards for her performances.
 
• Apart from playback singing, Neeti is actively involved in live performances and has represented India on international platforms.

questions.question: Kathak dancer Birju Maharaj received India's second highest civilian honour, the Padma Vibhushan, in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1986**__.

questions.question:
Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?

Nucleus - Storage of genetic information

Ribosome - Protein synthesis

Lysosome - Suicidal bags

Mitochondria - Lipid metabolism
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria - Lipid metabolism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nucleus - Storage of genetic information:**

 
 
• The nucleus is the control center of the cell and contains the cell's genetic material in the form of DNA.
 
• It regulates gene expression and mediates the replication of DNA during the cell cycle.
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
 
 
• **Ribosome - Protein synthesis:**
 
 
• Ribosomes are responsible for synthesizing proteins by translating messenger RNA (mRNA) into amino acid sequences.
 
• They are found floating in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum (referred to as rough ER).
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
 
 
• **Lysosome - Suicidal bags:**
 
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes capable of breaking down cellular debris and waste.
 
• They are often referred to as "suicidal bags" because they can digest the cell itself in case of severe damage or infection.
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria - Lipid metabolism:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are known as the "powerhouses of the cell" because they are primarily responsible for cellular respiration and energy production in the form of ATP.
 
• While mitochondria play a role in lipid metabolism, they are not primarily responsible for lipid metabolism. Lipid metabolism predominantly occurs in the **smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER)** and the cytoplasm.
 
• This statement is **incorrect**, as mitochondria are not the primary site for lipid metabolism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nucleus:**

 
 
• The nucleus contains chromosomes, which are made up of DNA and proteins. DNA holds the instructions for making proteins, which determine the structure and function of the cell.
 
• The nucleus also contains a smaller structure called the nucleolus, which is involved in ribosome production.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes:**
 
 
• They can be found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, though their structure differs slightly between the two types.
 
• Ribosomes are made up of RNA and proteins and are essential for translating genetic information into functional proteins.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes:**
 
 
• They contain hydrolytic enzymes that digest unwanted cellular materials, including damaged organelles and pathogens.
 
• Lysosomes are essential for maintaining cellular health and recycling cellular components, a process known as autophagy.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are double-membraned organelles responsible for producing adenosine triphosphate (**ATP**), the energy currency of the cell, through oxidative phosphorylation.
 
• They also play an important role in cell signaling, cellular differentiation, and apoptosis (programmed cell death).
 
• While mitochondria are involved in some steps of lipid metabolism, such as fatty acid β-oxidation, the smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the primary site for lipid synthesis and metabolism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other key organelles in a cell:**

 
 
• **Golgi apparatus:** Modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids for storage or transport out of the cell.
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):**
 
 
• **Rough ER:** Studded with ribosomes and involved in protein synthesis and modification.
 
• **Smooth ER:** Synthesizes lipids, metabolizes carbohydrates, and detoxifies drugs and poisons.
 
 
 
• **Peroxisomes:** Break down fatty acids and detoxify harmful substances.
 
• **Chloroplasts (in plant cells):** Sites of photosynthesis where sunlight is converted into chemical energy.
 
 
 
• **Functions of lipids in the cell:**
 
 
• Serve as energy storage molecules.
 
• Act as structural components of cell membranes (phospholipids).
 
• Play a role in cell signaling and as precursors for hormones.

questions.question: 'Abhinaya Darpana' by Nandikesvara is one of the main sources of textual material for the study of the technique and grammar of body movement in the __________dance.

__
 
• **Abhinaya Darpana** is a highly regarded text authored by **Nandikesvara**, focusing on the art of expression in classical Indian dance.
 
• The text serves as one of the foundational sources for understanding the **technique and grammar of body movements** in classical Indian dance forms, particularly **Bharatanatyam**.
 
• It elaborates on different aspects of dance, such as **mudras (hand gestures), postures, and facial expressions**, which are integral to classical dance performances. *Hence, Bharatanatyam is directly linked to this text.*
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest and most prominent classical dance forms of India, deeply rooted in Tamil Nadu's culture and tradition. Its techniques align closely with the principles described in the **Abhinaya Darpana**.
 
• The dance is known for its rigorous footwork, precise hand gestures, and expressive facial movements, all of which are extensively discussed in **Nandikesvara's text**. *Hence, Bharatanatyam is the correct answer.*
 
• Other classical dance forms like **Manipuri, Odissi, and Kathak** have their own distinctive styles and techniques. While they may share certain elements with Bharatanatyam, they are not primarily associated with the **Abhinaya Darpana**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Bharatanatyam.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **About Abhinaya Darpana:**

 
 
• **Abhinaya Darpana** is a crucial text authored by **Nandikesvara**, focusing on the art of expression and the grammar of body movements.

• **Bharatanatyam:**

• **Features:** It is characterized by intricate footwork, elaborate hand gestures, and expressive facial movements.
 
• **Application:** Traditionally performed in temples as a form of devotion, it has evolved into a popular stage art.

• **Odissi:** Originated in **Odisha**, known for its lyrical movements and strong connection to temple sculptures.
 
• **Kathak:** Originated in **North India**, characterized by storytelling through rhythmic footwork and spins.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
